executiveSummary: GM0406 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but is not a calibrated Huizen first-72-hour forecast. The canonical major-river preset assigns a persistent 0.464497 legacy flood amplitude and 3,105 affected people-equivalent through T+72 without a Rhine, Meuse or IJssel pathway. Official Huizen and AGV evidence instead identifies a distinct Gooimeer mechanism: low areas and direct open connections, a +0.80 m NAP extreme-water design reference at Kalmoes, and actual January 2024 operation of the Huizen sluices, pump, culvert and weir. That managed lake pathway is absent from the coastal preset, whose direct water is zero, and from any auditable defence/event state. Eight unrelated non-earthquake presets reuse the same top-five neighbourhood hazard order, while wildfire reports zero direct fire despite Huizen's named heath and woodland interface. Public utility, water, transport, telecom, education and cross-boundary hospital records add context but not live capacity or restoration. Suppress unsupported major-river impacts; retain Gooimeer, pluvial, wildfire, utility and acute-care states as Unknown until versioned causal evidence is selected. Unknown and NoData are never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0406 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; BAG/PDOK and BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM0406 as Huizen and report 41,196 residents, density 2,606 per square kilometre, 26.5% aged 65 or older and 6,874 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable fields retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [5.230605133613082, 52.291324133638376] lies inside the 2025 generalized polygon. BAG supplies one active woonplaats, Huizen, under Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT supplies Bikbergen, Crailo, Huizen and Huizerhoogt as named woonkernen, which are settlement labels rather than four separately measured resident totals.

The 30 neighbourhood populations sum to 41,215, 19 above the municipal total (+0.046%); the generated allocation reconciles exactly to 41,196. Registers do not measure event-time visitors, heath/forest recreation, harbour users, commuters, hospital patients, home-care dependency or household stocks.

evidenceSources.title: NWB, rail and scheduled public-transport inputs for Huizen
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates seven logical links: four A1 edges to Laren, Blaricum, Gooise Meren and Hilversum, two N527 edges to Blaricum and Hilversum, and one N526 edge to Blaricum. The four A1 edges share physicalCorridorId NWB-road-1 and the two N527 edges share NWB-road-527; series/junction edges and generalized 260/150 capacities are non-additive scenario ceilings, not measured throughput.

No ProRail station is inside GM0406. GTFS preprocessing finds 45 stop areas, while the municipality confirms bus travel to Gooise Meren, Blaricum, Hilversum and Amsterdam. Geometry and schedules do not establish event-time operation, evacuation throughput, fuel, staffing, hospital access or restoration.
No current NDW situation in the deployment's 2 September 2026 bounded snapshot is assigned to GM0406. That is a time/coverage result and cannot be interpreted as every road or bus route being open.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Gooi en Vechtstreek 2024
supports: The definitive regional profile prioritizes storm/wind/precipitation, cold, heat, flooding and nature fire, as well as electricity outage, speech/data outage and cyberattack. It says nature fire became a priority because climate change raises probability and impact.

The profile is regional planning evidence, not a GM0406 hazard footprint, real-time warning, impact curve, resource assignment or action-completion record. No blanket machine reuse licence was stated in the document inspected.
Regional prioritization supports scenario inclusion, but cannot validate the simulator's exact neighbourhood ranking, service percentages, affected people-equivalent or recovery curve.

evidenceSources.title: Water- en rioleringsprogramma 2026–2030, local water-system facts and Kalmoes development conditions
evidenceSources.edition: WRP 2026–2030 and current official pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Huizen's current programme covers wastewater, rainwater and groundwater and commits to maintenance, separation, water-nuisance/drought measures and climate adaptation. The official Soorten water in Huizen PDF lists 80 km mixed sewer, 160 km separated sewer, 26 km pressure main, 88 pressure-sewer pumps, 18 sewer pumps, three collection pumps, 45 km drainage and 63 monitoring wells; inventory does not prove event-time function or spare capacity.

The Kalmoes project page says the site is low at about +0.90 m NAP, Huizen is not currently protected by a water barrier because it is categorized as high ground, and there are direct open connections to the Gooimeer. It uses +0.80 m NAP as an extreme Gooimeer water reference and requires raising terrain/floors; this project-specific design evidence is not a municipal inundation map.

The same page identifies eastern Huizen as a seepage area fed from the Utrechtse Heuvelrug and requires at least 60 mm per square metre storage for new/renewed hard surface. The Stad en Lande project page reports increasing water nuisance in a local climate stress test. Neither page supplies a live drainage or municipality-wide pluvial result; no blanket reuse licence was stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Amstel, Gooi en Vecht / Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat / WMCN
evidenceSources.title: Huizen high-water response, public water assets, Waterinfo and LIWO routes
evidenceSources.edition: AGV January 2024 event page; HWH/Waterinfo snapshots 2–3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: During January 2024 high Gooimeer/Markermeer water, AGV closed and reinforced the Huizen sluice doors, installed a pump, closed a culvert and raised a weir, then monitored conditions. This proves an operated lake/interface pathway, not that the same action, protection or outcome applies to a future event.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH collections contain 17 GM0406 points: one RWZI, three surface-water pumps, one barrier sluice and 12 weirs. All 17 capacities are null; 16 name AGV and the RWZI uses generic manager 'Waterschap'. The municipal sewer inventory is much larger, so HWH points are explicitly partial context, not a complete drainage network.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0406 in the bounded snapshots. Waterinfo observations are generally ten-minute CC0 public guidance and forecast coverage declines to zero national records at the requested T+72 water-level window; absence locally is NoData/coverage, never normal water or safety.

LIWO release 2025.1.6 at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows is an irregular expert scenario library. A governed run must retain release/scenario, Gooimeer boundary level/hydrograph and datum, wind, barrier/defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, per-layer licence, coverage and NoData; LIWO is not live observation.

evidenceSources.title: Huizen heath/woodland interface and current nature-fire evidence semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Current area and fire-risk pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Goois Natuurreservaat locates the 73-hectare Tafelbergheide in Blaricum and Huizen and identifies it as heath; Huizer Eng is a 34-hectare Huizen transition of fields and woodland edges, and Bikbergen is 55 hectares of connected woodland, fields and estates. These public pages establish fuel/visitor context but not an ignition, flame front or smoke plume.

The official national nature-fire page says risk rises in forest, heath and grass during longer dry periods and the region's phase is assessed from weather, manager, field and expert information. A displayed phase is time-varying operational context, not a 72-hour deterministic fire spread forecast.

GNR reported on 11 August 2026 that prolonged drought was stressing higher Gooise ridge soils and that nature-fire danger was very high. That dated observation must not be projected to other valid times, and no blanket reuse licence was stated on the pages.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Public provider territories, grid planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Provider/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1
supports: The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS identifies Liander electricity/gas, PWN drinking water and Ziggo media at the municipal reference point; provider dates range from September 2025 to March 2026 and drainage returns empty. A single-point territory result is not municipality-wide completeness, topology, outage, water quality, capacity or restoration.

The single sampled Liander area OS HUIZEN 10-1i reports 36 MW existing/required withdrawal plus 3.2 MW and 25 queued requests, 36 MW existing/20 MW required injection plus 25 MW queued, and 28 projects earliest 2026. NBNL planning is at least quarterly and queues monthly; its exact dataset licence was not found. It is not current load, household availability, reserve or T+72 state.

RDI WFS returns 48 antenna sites, including 22 mobile and two fixed-link sites; no fixed refresh or reuse licence was stated. Daily DUO RIO under CC BY (version unspecified) returns 23 education records. These do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, shelter role, occupancy, staff, supplies or live status.

RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026 under CC0, assigns no acute-care facility to GM0406. It identifies Tergooi MC in GM0402 Hilversum as 24/7 SEH plus acute obstetrics with 17 reported rooms and 26,161 2025 visits. Empty local count is not no care need; annual registration is not live acceptance or capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Tergooi MC / Nationaal Coördinator Terrorismebestrijding en Veiligheid
evidenceSources.title: Cross-boundary emergency care and national first-72-hour preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current official pages inspected 3 September 2026; NCTV information booklet publication 4 March 2026
supports: Tergooi states its 24-hour emergency department is at Laan van Tergooi 2 in Hilversum and that all 24/7 emergency hospital care moved from Blaricum to Hilversum in May 2023. This establishes a cross-boundary dependency for Huizen, not live acceptance, beds, staffing, generator/fuel endurance, oxygen, medicines or route availability.

NCTV's Denk vooruit guidance at https://www.denkvooruit.nl/informatieboekje says households should plan to manage 72 hours through a kit, plan and mutual help; it recommends three litres of water per person per day. It also says incidents can last longer and responders cannot be everywhere at once.

Preparedness advice is not a measurement that 44% or any fraction of Huizen households has stocks, nor a guarantee that aid, utilities, transport or care recover at T+72. No machine event/action feed or blanket reuse licence was identified on these public guidance pages.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM0406 is uniquely Huizen in Noord-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Gooi en Vechtstreek.
Boundary/statistics editions are 2025; current pages, 2024 high water, 2026 registers and the synthetic exercise clock remain separate.
The reference point is contained and no headline mismatch was found.

geography.summary: The municipal and regional geometry is coherent, but high-ground/low-area, Gooimeer, drainage and heath/woodland pathways require source geometry.
notes: Official evidence distinguishes high Gooise ridge terrain from lower eastern/harbour areas, direct Gooimeer connections and managed sluice/pump/weir interfaces.
A municipal reference-point distance or shared neighbourhood seed cannot replace lake connectivity, barrier state, AHN/BGT drainage or forest/heath geometry.
Every LIWO, HWH, climate-test and land-cover layer requires its own edition, valid time, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData mask.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and neighbourhood rounding is explicitly reconciled.
notes: Population 41,196, density 2,606, age65Pct 26.5 and one-person households 6,874 agree.
Neighbourhood population sums to 41,215 (+19); the deterministic allocation reconciles to 41,196. Published households total 18,795 and age65+ rows total 10,920.
The high older-resident share is planning context, not a count of people needing evacuation, cooling, medicines or care.

regionalDetail.summary: All 30 neighbourhoods load, but published attributes, water inventory coverage and every operational state are incomplete.
notes: District heat and charging are missing for 30/30 neighbourhoods; home value, housing/tenure and benefit fields for three; cars per household for six; doctor/supermarket distance and density for one. Null is not zero.

HWH provides 17 context points, every capacity null, while Huizen's own system fact sheet lists substantially more sewer/drainage infrastructure. Neither list proves topology, condition, backup or spare capacity.
Provider, planning, antenna, education and acute-care records do not establish event-time availability.

settlements.summary: One BAG woonplaats and four BRT woonkernen are retained under their different source semantics.
notes: Huizen is the single active BAG woonplaats; BRT additionally labels Bikbergen, Crailo and Huizerhoogt as woonkernen.
Do not duplicate municipal population across settlement labels or interpret a named nature-adjacent core as a measured emergency population.
Visitor and recreation occupancy in harbour, beach, forest and heath areas remains Unknown.

transport.summary: A1/N527/N526, bus and rail-less context are reproducible, but southern junction edges and event-time access remain unresolved.
notes: Seven logical boundary edges connect four neighbours, but four A1 edges and two N527 edges respectively share single physical corridors and are non-additive.
NWB represents only mobility and assumed road-logistics supply; it never becomes utility, hospital or facility topology.
Huizen has no station and depends on buses/roads for Hilversum, including Tergooi; event-time N527/A1/A27 connecting access, bus service and hospital acceptance are Unknown.
Empty bounded NDW output is not an all-open assertion.

emergencyContext.summary: Priority risks, high-water measures, 72-hour guidance and cross-boundary care are identified, but no auditable local action/resource state exists.
notes: The January 2024 response names concrete sluice, pump, culvert and weir actions, but the simulator has no event trigger, responsible authority, resource, state or completion record.
Tergooi Hilversum is a critical cross-boundary dependency, not guaranteed capacity; access, power, water, telecom, staffing, oxygen, medicines and acceptance remain Unknown.

Required action categories include warning, lake/barrier control, welfare/evacuation, pluvial/drainage action, nature-fire/smoke response, roads/buses, hospital continuity, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.
National 72-hour advice is not measured Huizen preparedness or a recovery deadline.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: Mandatory and focused gates covered ten presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Outputs are synthetic exercise indices; affected people-equivalent is not observed people/casualties and person-hours is cumulative weighted local pre-network service shortfall versus a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0406 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across the complete matrix.
Intensity-zero event effects are zero, repeat runs and UI/core presets agree, and local allocation reconciles exactly.
Service-layer selection preserves physical hazard, route ceilings hold and event-attributable person-hours is monotonic.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A false persistent major-river result and shared neighbourhood ordering contradict Huizen's lake, drainage and nature pathways.
notes: River T+24 and T+72 both apply legacy flood amplitude 0.464497, severity 0.143321 and 3,105 affected people-equivalent without a named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach, boundary condition, defence or connected footprint.
The coastal preset has zero direct water while official evidence shows a separately typed Gooimeer/barrier pathway; zero is scoped model output, not an all-clear.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the T+24 order Flevo, Huizermaat Zuid, Huizermaat Noord, Bijvanck Noord and Parrewijn. This does not follow the named low-water, drainage, population-vulnerability or heath/woodland geometry.

Wildfire has zero direct fire but 0.465350 smoke and 0.709290 drought at T+24, affecting 800 people-equivalent without ignition, fuel, spread, wind/plume or valid-time phase. Tafelberger Heide is not in the top five.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are inspectable but not calibrated to Huizen providers, drainage, transport, acute care or nature/lake operations.
notes: River T+24/T+72 availability is power 0.802519, water 0.767058, drainage 0.699363, gas 0.847416, telecom 0.746886, mobility 0.921451, facilities 0.723353 and supply 0.944228; no operator validates these persistent values.
Liander/PWN/Ziggo territory, one NBNL sample, HWH points and RDI sites remain non-causal context.
No acute-care facility is inside GM0406; Tergooi registration in Hilversum does not establish road acceptance, backup utilities, staff or incident capacity.
Sensitive or unavailable topology must use explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, never invented public precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes are present but unresolved water body, defence, target, fire and operational dimensions are not declared.
notes: River and coastal report derived-screening, and compound reports synthetic with unsupportedDimensions=[], despite no named river/lake event, level/datum, barrier state, footprint, arrival/recession or dewatering condition.
The legacy field floodDepthM must not be presented as surveyed metres; the river value is unsupported direct water for this preset.
Wildfire lacks ignition/fuel/spread/plume and cyber lacks a target. Current, 2024-event, planning/register and synthetic T+72 valid times cannot be fused.
Empty Waterinfo, NDW, drainage-provider and local acute-care results must become explicit NoData/Unknown, not normal, open, safe or available.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river and compound outcomes and all exact recovery values lack local water, operator, hospital or action evidence.
notes: River is unchanged from T+24 to T+72 at severity 0.143321, pressure 0.193494 and 3,105 affected; person-hours rise to 514,032.23. No boundary hydrograph, barrier state, recession, pumping or repair evidence supports this plateau.
Compound T+72 severity/pressure/affected/person-hours is 0.553729/0.544212/23,461/1,647,193.22; all eight service availability values remain exactly at their T+24 plateau.
Storm, pluvial, winter and wildfire direct severity return to zero by T+72 but exact residual service values still lack operator action/restoration evidence.

No sluice/pump decision, dewatering, utility crew, route reopening, Tergooi acceptance, household stock or confirmed intervention supports the curves; 72 hours is a preparedness horizon, not an all-recovered promise.

findings.summary: The major-river preset fabricates persistent direct flooding in Huizen.
findings.evidence: River T+24 and T+72 both report legacy flood amplitude 0.464497 and 3,105 affected people-equivalent. No named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach, hydrograph, defence or connected footprint supports it; official local water evidence describes Gooimeer and regional drainage mechanisms instead.
findings.action: Suppress GM0406 direct river flood severity, affected population and attributable service effects in this preset. Keep indirect national-network effects separately typed; only enable direct water after a versioned named hydraulic scenario intersects the municipality.

findings.summary: Real Gooimeer high-water and barrier operation has no selectable causal scenario.
findings.evidence: AGV closed/reinforced Huizen sluices, installed a pump, closed a culvert and raised a weir in January 2024. Huizen documents low terrain/direct Gooimeer connections and +0.80 m NAP as a project design reference, while canonical coastal direct water is zero and no barrier state exists.
findings.action: Add a separately typed IJsselmeergebied/Gooimeer high-water scenario driven by time-aligned RWS/WMCN boundary data or expert LIWO selection. Require level/hydrograph and datum, wind, barrier/defence state, connected footprint, arrival/recession, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData; zero coastal sea water remains scoped, not safe.

findings.summary: A shared neighbourhood multiplier replaces hazard-specific Huizen geometry.
findings.evidence: Eight non-earthquake presets reuse Flevo, Huizermaat Zuid, Huizermaat Noord, Bijvanck Noord and Parrewijn as the T+24 top five. That order does not encode Gooimeer connectivity, the low east, Stad en Lande drainage evidence, vulnerable population, or Tafelbergheide/Bikbergen/Huizer Eng fuels.
findings.action: Remove shared local hazard ranking. Render unresolved municipal amplitude uniformly or Unknown until each hazard has a versioned surface; add tests that lake, pluvial, heat and wildfire ranks follow their own source geometry and differ when evidence differs.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth and impact precision lacks sewer, terrain and groundwater calibration.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports legacy flood amplitude 0.486557 and 5,956 affected people-equivalent. Huizen publishes mixed/separated sewer and drainage inventories, 60 mm development storage rules and a Stad en Lande stress-test signal, but none supplies the model's rainfall surface, capacity, condition or footprint.
findings.action: Integrate a municipality/AGV climate stress-test or 3Di result with hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, saturation/groundwater, resolution, edition/licence and NoData. Until then label depth, ranking and affected count synthetic/unsupported rather than local prediction.

findings.summary: Wildfire smoke is generated without ignition, spread or Huizen's known heath/woodland interface.
findings.evidence: Wildfire T+24 has direct fire 0, smoke 0.465350, drought 0.709290 and 800 affected people-equivalent. Regional policy prioritizes nature fire and authoritative pages locate Tafelbergheide, Bikbergen and Huizer Eng, yet the model contains no ignition, fuels, wind/plume, visitor state or time-valid risk phase.
findings.action: Require an explicit exercise ignition and versioned BRT/manager fuel extent, time-aligned weather, spread/smoke method and NoData before local direct/fire-plume claims. Keep daily phase and dated drought observations as valid-time context only; zero fire is not zero smoke risk and synthetic smoke is not observed exposure.

findings.summary: Exact utility and restoration percentages have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Eight precise river and compound availability values come from generic dependencies. Liander/PWN/Ziggo territory, one NBNL planning sample, HWH assets and RDI sites provide no outage, topology, backup, switching, water quality, crew or repair state; drainage provider lookup is empty.
findings.action: Keep public context affectsSimulation=false and label operational values aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Accept only authorized time-scoped operator aggregates, preserve manual incident-override provenance, and never render empty provider/asset/telemetry results as zero, normal or available.

findings.summary: Water-control points are useful context but demonstrably partial and non-operational.
findings.evidence: Seventeen HWH points include the Huizen barrier sluice and RWZI, but every capacity is null. Huizen's own document lists 88 pressure-sewer pumps, 18 sewer pumps and three collection pumps absent as corresponding deployed point types; no local Waterinfo point is assigned.
findings.action: Retain points, manager labels, nulls, source collection, retrieval, licence and partial-coverage warning. Seek AGV/Huizen-authorized catchment/control aggregates; never sum assets or infer function, spare capacity or safety from registration/absence.

findings.summary: Seven southern-corner logical road edges do not equal seven independent evacuation or hospital corridors.
findings.evidence: Four A1 edges share one physical corridor and two N527 edges share one corridor; Huizen has no station and relies on road/bus connections to Hilversum and Tergooi. Empty bounded NDW is not proof of passability.
findings.action: Retain NWB only for mobility/supply with physical-corridor non-additivity. Add event-time critical junction, N527/A1/A27 connector, bus and Tergooi destination state from official feeds or command input; otherwise show throughput, passability and acceptance Unknown.

findings.summary: Cross-boundary Tergooi dependency is not represented as first-72-hour access and acceptance state.
findings.evidence: RIVM contains zero GM0406 acute-care points and identifies the 24/7 SEH/acute-obstetric service at Tergooi in Hilversum; Tergooi says all 24/7 emergency hospital care moved there from Blaricum in 2023. Annual records do not establish incident acceptance, beds, staff, backup or travel.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate facility role, live acceptance/diversion, road/ambulance access, backup/fuel, critical utilities/supplies and transfer status with valid time. Empty local facility count remains cross-boundary dependency, not no demand; absent operational fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger represents Huizen's documented controls and dependencies.
findings.evidence: Official sources name prior high-water controls, regional priority risks, providers, bus/road links, a remote SEH and household guidance, but the simulation ingests no trigger, authority, assignment, resources, status or completion.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for warning, sluice/pump/culvert/weir decisions, low-area welfare/evacuation, drainage, nature-fire/smoke, road/bus control, Tergooi continuity/transfer, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repairs and mutual aid. Actions affect recovery only after confirmed status and provenance.

corrections.summary: Suppress false GM0406 major-river inundation while preserving separately unresolved Gooimeer and indirect-network risk.
corrections.validation: The canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel river preset yields zero GM0406 direct flood and direct affected population with an explicit unsupported-pathway note; no false service loss is attributed to that direct water, and separate lake/regional/pluvial risks remain Unknown rather than safe.

corrections.summary: Introduce governed Gooimeer/managed-barrier scenario semantics instead of overloading sea-coastal or major-river presets.
corrections.validation: No precise Huizen lake impact appears without a named RWS/WMCN/LIWO event; supported fixtures preserve level/hydrograph, datum, wind, barrier/defence state, footprint, arrival/recession, probability, version, licence, coverage and NoData.

corrections.summary: Replace common neighbourhood ranking with hazard-specific lake, pluvial, heat and nature-fire geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated presets no longer share one top-five order; Gooimeer fixtures follow connected low-area geometry, pluvial fixtures retain sewer/groundwater semantics, and wildfire fixtures intersect explicit heath/woodland fuels and plume evidence.

corrections.summary: Keep HWH/provider/grid/antenna/education/acute-care records context-only with strict Unknown and NoData semantics.
corrections.validation: Cards/exports show publisher, edition, retrieval/valid time, licence, coverage and affectsSimulation=false; null HWH capacities and empty Waterinfo, NDW, drainage-provider and local acute-care outputs never render as zero, normal, safe, open or available.

corrections.summary: Represent Tergooi access and Huizen's first-72-hour authorities/actions with an Unknown-first ledger.
corrections.validation: At every checkpoint lake control, warning/welfare, drainage/fire response, roads/buses, hospital acceptance/transfer, reception/resupply and utility repairs show authority, trigger, assignment, resource, state, source and valid time; absent facts remain Unknown and only confirmed actions affect recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish Liander/PWN/gas/telecom/drainage topology, current control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.

Gooimeer impact depends on lake level, wind setup, direct connections, sluice/barrier and pumping state, local elevation and recession; a 2024 response or project design level is not a current forecast.
The municipal sewer fact sheet and HWH point layer have different coverage and semantics; neither proves hydraulic connectivity, condition, comparable capacity or operation.
Nature-fire phase, drought, ignition, fuels, visitors, wind and smoke change rapidly; static area pages and a dated warning cannot calibrate another scenario valid time.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO/RIVM records omit visitors, harbour/beach/nature occupancy, commuters, home-care needs, live Tergooi load, shelters and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, road, warning and facility states may change after audit completion; stale or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Define province-wide IJsselmeer/Markermeer/Gooimeer lake-flood semantics distinct from North Sea coastal surge and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel major-river flooding, including direct open connections and managed barriers.

Reconcile Huizen, Blaricum, Gooise Meren and adjacent Flevoland shore pathways through a single versioned RWS/WMCN/LIWO/AGV evidence contract without treating high-ground classification as blanket protection.
Suppress the GM0406 major-river false positive and test other Gooi municipalities for the same distance-screening defect.
Test repeated neighbourhood ranking across Noord-Holland lake, urban-pluvial, heat and heath/woodland contexts; require hazard-specific geometry and NoData masks.
Audit A1/N527/N526/A27 connectors, bus dependence and Tergooi Hilversum access without double-counting shared NWB corridors or converting schedules/facilities into guaranteed availability.
Require Unknown-first 72-hour actions for water-control assets, nature fire/smoke, cross-boundary acute care, temporary water, evacuation/reception and household preparedness.
